title: Torta della nonna
subtitle: Italian shortcrust tart filled with lemon custard and scattered with pine nuts
excerpt: Torta della nonna is an Italian tart of two layers of shortcrust pastry with a lemon-scented custard filling and pine nuts scattered over the top before baking. The pastry goes in the tin raw, the custard is spooned in cold, and a second pastry lid goes on before it all bakes together. The custard sets to a soft, just-firm filling inside the crisp, buttery pastry.
sourceNotes: Torta della nonna is a traditional Italian tart associated with Tuscany, whose name means grandmother's tart. Documented in Italian regional cookbooks from the twentieth century and a standard home-baking recipe throughout central Italy.

glossaryTerms.definition: Italian custard cream made from egg yolks, sugar, cornflour, and milk, cooked until thick. The base filling for many Italian pastries and tarts.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best served the day it is made, or the day after at room temperature. Keep at room temperature for up to 2 days; refrigerate if the kitchen is warm.

content.text: Torta della nonna is an Italian double-pastry tart with a lemon

filling and a scattering of pine nuts on top. The pastry is rich and crumbly from the egg yolks and icing sugar in the dough. The custard goes in cold and bakes to a just-set filling inside the crisp pastry shell.

items.prepNote: cold and diced, for the pastry

content.text: Rub the cold butter into the flour and icing sugar until the mixture looks like breadcrumbs. Add the egg yolks and mix until a dough just comes together. Divide into two pieces, one slightly larger than the other. Flatten each into a disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.

Whisk the egg yolks, caster sugar, cornflour, and lemon zest together in a bowl. Bring the milk and vanilla to just below the boil in a medium saucepan, then pour slowly over the egg mixture, whisking as you go.

Return to the saucepan and cook over a medium heat, stirring constantly, until thick and just beginning to bubble. Remove from the heat immediately. Press cling film directly onto the surface and leave to cool.

Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Roll the larger disc to about 4 mm thick and use it to line a 23 cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Press firmly into the edges and trim any overhang.
Spoon the cooled custard into the tart case and spread level. Roll the second disc to fit the top and lay it over the custard. Press the edges together to seal, trimming any excess pastry.
Scatter the pine nuts over the top and press them lightly into the pastry. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is golden and the top is firm to the touch.
Leave to cool in the tin for 30 minutes before removing. Dust with icing sugar before serving.

attrs.problem: Pastry shrinking in the tin during baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid stretching the pastry when lining the tin; stretched dough contracts in the oven.
attrs.fix: Press the pastry into the tin rather than pulling it. Leave a 5 mm overhang when trimming and let it shrink onto the edge of the tin rather than below it.

attrs.problem: Custard filling liquid when sliced after cooling
attrs.avoid: Avoid using custard that is still too warm when it goes into the tart; warm custard steams and delays the set.
attrs.fix: Cool the custard until it is completely cold and firm before spooning it into the pastry case.
